artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a closed set $E \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ a weak Arakelian set if, for every function $g: E \to \mathbb{C}$ that is continuous on $E$ and analytic in the interior of $E$, there exists an entire function $f: \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that, for every sequence $\{z_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of points of $E$,
$$|f(z_n)| \to \infty \quad \text{if and only if} \quad |g(z_n)| \to \infty.$$
Find a purely geometric (or topological) characterisation of the closed subsets $E$ of $\mathbb{C}$ that are weak Arakelian sets.
artifact.status_search_result: Rubel posed the problem of geometrically characterising weak Arakelian sets in 1976. Partial results exist (e.g., an example of an Arakelian glove that is a weak Arakelian set, Stray, Illinois J. Math. 1983), and recent work continues to study related characterizations of (standard) Arakelian sets, but no complete geometric characterization of weak Arakelian sets appears in the literature. The problem is generally regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: An example of an Arakelian glove which is a weak Arakelian set
status_evidence.snippet: In 1976 L. A. Rubel posed the problem of characterising weak Arakelian sets, or at least showing whether or not there exists an Arakelian glove which is weak Arakelian.
status_evidence.claim: Documents the original Rubel problem and provides a partial result (an example), suggesting full characterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: A logarithmic characterization of Arakelian sets
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work giving characterizations of (standard) Arakelian sets.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity addresses Arakelian sets but does not resolve the weak Arakelian characterization.
